s21d1_033_compilation.how_it_was_verified: ExperienceCompilerService.compile was called twice per trajectory. The second call reads the persisted manifest from PostgreSQL, recompiles from the sources, and raises 'persisted manifest differs from deterministic recompilation' on any difference. Nothing raised, so a freshly compiled manifest equalled the stored one on all 40.

restart_proof.method: a separate process opened a new engine against the D1 database and resolved every manifest by compilation identity

s21d1_033_compilation.contrast_with_w3a: The 60 historical coding pairs are source_resolution_only because their wall-clock manifests cannot be recompiled at all. The 20 fresh pairs are verified by actual recompilation against the persisted manifest.

limitation.what_was_not_proven: recompilation from persisted sources inside a fresh process
limitation.why: PostgresExperienceRepository exposes get_manifest and list_candidates but no source reader, so rebuilding a SourceResolverRegistry from the 280 persisted experience_sources rows would need a loader that does not exist. Building one speculatively is not in D1 scope.
limitation.what_was_proven_instead: the recompilation equality check ran against the manifest as read back from PostgreSQL, which is the byte-identity gate the repository itself defines, and a fresh process resolved all 40 manifests with identical hashes
limitation.resume_idempotency: compilation identity is uuid5 over the trajectory digest and create_compilation uses on_conflict_do_nothing, so re-offering the same trajectory is a no-op. A re-execution produces a different trajectory and therefore a different compilation, which the selection manifest records as intended behaviour rather than a defect.
